headline: Two arrested after scrap dealer killed over financial dispute in Tejgaon
summary: RAB-2 has apprehended the main suspect and an accomplice in the murder of a scrap dealer near the FDC gate in Dhaka.
details: RAB-2 has arrested two suspects, including the primary accused, in connection with the murder of a scrap dealer named Selim. The arrests were made during an operation in the Karwan Bazar area of Dhaka on Tuesday morning.

The incident occurred on July 19 around 3:00 PM near the old FDC gate in Tejgaon. Following a financial dispute over scrap business transactions, Selim was reportedly attacked with a sharp knife and critically injured.

Selim was rushed to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Following the murder, the victim's wife, Rekha Begum, filed a murder case with the Tejgaon Industrial Area Police Station, naming five suspects.
According to RAB, the arrested individuals are Mokbul, alias Mukul Sohag (27), and Mizanur Rahman Mizan (39). The victim's mobile phone was recovered from Mizan's possession during the arrest.
Investigations reveal that the attack was carried out under the orders of another suspect named Ratan, who is still at large. RAB is continuing operations to capture him.
The arrested suspects have criminal records. Mizan faces five cases including robbery and drug-related offenses, while Mokbul has three cases including drugs and attempted robbery.

headline: Satkhira: River erosion threatens 200-year-old Budhhata Market
summary: A historic marketplace in Satkhira is at risk of being lost to the river as erosion continues to eat away at the land.
details: The 200-year-old Budhhata Market in Satkhira is facing a severe threat from river erosion.
The river's current is steadily eating away at the banks, bringing the water closer to the historic market structures.
Local residents and traders are concerned about the loss of this long-standing commercial hub and the heritage it represents.
Authorities are urged to take immediate action to protect the market and prevent further land loss.
